title: Worksheet — Locating Places on the Earth (Class 6 CBSE)
instructions: Attempt all 10 questions. Show working for the subjective questions. Total time: 30 minutes.

questions.question: The 0° latitude line is called the:
The Earth is a perfect sphere.
questions.explanation: It's an oblate spheroid (slightly flattened sphere).

questions.question: The Prime Meridian passes through ____, near London.
The Tropic of Cancer is at:
The hottest heat zone (between the two tropics) is the:
List the five most important parallels and their latitude values.
questions.answer: Equator (0°), Tropic of Cancer (23½° N), Tropic of Capricorn (23½° S), Arctic Circle (66½° N), Antarctic Circle (66½° S). Plus the poles at 90° N and 90° S.

questions.question: Find the place at coordinates (28.6° N, 77.2° E). State the city, hemisphere, and heat zone.
questions.answer: City: New Delhi. Hemispheres: Northern + Eastern. Heat zone: Torrid (since latitude < 23½° N — actually 28.6° N is just north of the Tropic of Cancer, so it lies in the southern part of the north Temperate zone). Either Torrid or Temperate accepted depending on the boundary read; New Delhi is just inside the Temperate zone.

questions.question: The Earth turns 360° in 24 hours. How many degrees per hour? Per minute?
questions.answer: Per hour: 360 / 24 = 15° per hour. Per minute: 15 / 60 = 0.25° per minute (or 1° in 4 minutes).

questions.question: When it is 9 am at Greenwich (0°), what time is it at 75° E?
questions.answer: 75° east → 75/15 = 5 hours ahead. 9 am + 5 h = 2 pm at 75° E.
questions.explanation: Apply 15° per hour; east is ahead.

questions.question: A new city has coordinates (35° N, 50° E). (i) Which hemispheres? (ii) Which heat zone? (iii) How many hours is it from India (75° E)?
questions.answer: (i) Northern + Eastern hemispheres. (ii) 35° N is between 23½° N and 66½° N, so it lies in the north Temperate zone. (iii) Difference in longitude with India = 75 − 50 = 25°. Time difference = 25 / 15 ≈ 1 h 40 min. India (east of this city) is ahead by ~1 h 40 min.

questions.question: Why does India use ONE standard time (IST = 82.5° E) although it spans many degrees of longitude?
questions.answer: India's longitude extends from about 68° E to 97° E — about 29° wide, which would naturally give ~2 hours of time difference between east and west. Using one time avoids confusion in trains, schools, broadcasting and government work. The trade-off: in eastern India the sun appears to rise earlier than the clock suggests, and in western India later. Many large countries (USA, Russia) use multiple time zones; India has chosen simplicity.
